result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A gives a title that names both the page and the club, and it points out that the buttons' source order doesn't match what's on screen, though it doesn't fix that. However, its block-level <nav> probably pushes the search box onto a new line, which is a visible change. B keeps the header layout intact by making the nav inline, but its title leaves out the club, it never mentions the button-order problem, and it adds overflow-wrap and minmax changes nobody asked for. Neither answer reorders the buttons. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers make nearly identical fixes for the skip link, h2 headings, button names and focus outline. Neither changes the source order of the buttons, which appear above the title on screen; B at least flags this. A wins because B wraps the links in a block-level <nav>, which pushes the search box onto a new line and visibly changes the layout the committee asked to keep. A sets its <nav> to inline, though its title leaves out the club name, which B includes.
